key_insight: Metal Sandbox combines isolated file access with native macOS execution to support concurrent AI agents writing Apple Metal GPU kernels. Its command-level scheduling approach targets GPU idle time between model requests, development commands, and kernel execution.
problem_solved: GPU-coding agents need native Apple Silicon tools, but their stop-and-start workflows leave accelerators idle. Running concurrent sessions also requires separating each agent’s file access.
method: Restrict file access per instance to separate concurrent agent workspaces.
Execute development commands natively on macOS for Apple Metal kernel workflows.
Introduce command-level scheduling to coordinate concurrent sessions; the supplied abstract is truncated before implementation details.
impact: This infrastructure could help practitioners train and evaluate Metal-kernel-generating models while making better use of local Apple Silicon GPUs. The provided excerpt does not include measured performance gains.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing isolated agent workspaces connected to native macOS tools and a shared GPU.
Session timelines distinguishing model requests, development commands, GPU execution, and idle periods.
Scheduling diagram illustrating how GPU work from concurrent sessions could fill idle gaps.
Shield, terminal, and GPU icons representing isolation, native execution, and accelerator use.
paper_title: Metal Sandbox: Isolated Execution and Command Scheduling for GPU Coding Agents on Apple Silicon
paper_authors: Haozhe Wang, Lina Chen, Fanqi Wan, Qi Han, Yinmin Zhang
